title: Process manifest
description: A server does not expose functions directly. It loads ONE manifest at a time, and the manifest selects which functions become visible tools. That is what keeps a large function catalogue from becoming a large tool surface — the catalogue is a deployment fact, the manifest is a runtime fact, and only the second one costs you anything.

id.description: Stable, kebab-case, never reused. Appears in every audit record.

version.description: Semver. Bump minor to add a tool; bump major to remove or change one.

trigger.description: What causes a person to run this. If you cannot name the moment, you have a capability rather than a process.

owner.description: The ROLE that presses the button — not a person's name. 'BIM coordinator', 'release engineer'.

deliverable.description: What exists afterwards that did not exist before.

acceptanceTest.description: THE LINE EVERYBODY LEAVES BLANK. How a non-technical reviewer confirms it worked, WITHOUT knowing how the result was produced. If you cannot write these, you do not have a process — you have a demo.

maxTools.description: The ceiling for THIS surface. Going over is a diagnosis, not a failure: it means two processes are sharing one manifest and nobody has separated them yet.

tools.description: Tool names visible when this manifest is loaded. Must not exceed maxTools.

services.description: Shared capability called BY tools and NEVER by the agent. Infrastructure has no tools, it has a contract — an agent that can call a service directly is holding a parts bin rather than running a process.

writes.description: Every write tool, with its preview partner. Generated as a PAIR or not generated. No convenience bypass — one bypass puts a hole in the audit trail nobody remembers.

blastRadius.description: The worst outcome of ONE confirmed call, in plain language.

idempotencyKey.description: Required on anything that CREATES. Derived from intent — never random, never a timestamp.

supportedVersions.description: An explicit LIST, never a range expression, and never narrowed in a minor release. Firms sit on a version for years and cannot upgrade mid-project.

tokenBudget.description: Measured, not estimated. If this is unknown the process is not done.

examples.name: Add-in Release Gate
examples.description: Validate, build, package and check an add-in before submission.
examples.trigger: A product is ready for submission, or a release branch is cut.
acceptanceTest: Every declared version in the matrix produced an installer.
The validation report lists zero blocking findings.
The privacy-policy URL in the manifest resolves with a 200.

writes.blastRadius: Writes files to the build output directory. No model, no remote system.
